=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): whorled (multiple leaves attached at the same node, visible in close-up images; at least 4 leaves emerging from a single node)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are grouped closely at the apex of the stem)

B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf has a single blade without subdivisions)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A

C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (smooth margin with no teeth or serrations visible)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): elliptic (broad in the middle, tapering toward both ends)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (tapering to a sharp point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): rounded (leaf base is gently curved, not tapering or heart-shaped)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (single midrib with lateral veins extending from it)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible, closely spaced, numerous (secondary veins are distinct and run parallel to each other, close together)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny (surface has a glossy appearance, reflecting light)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs or fuzz on leaf surface)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petiole is short, leaf blade appears to attach directly to stem)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petiole is round in cross-section, without wings or grooves)

D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (stem appears firm and brown, typical of young woody seedling)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on stem)
    19. Stem color: brown (stem is dark brown, with some green near the apex)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (surface appears smooth, no ridges or lenticels visible)

E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules visible at leaf bases)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no latex exudate visible)
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no pulvinus visible at leaf base)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils observed)

F. Notes: Multiple images show the same seedling from different angles; the leaf whorl is clearly visible in close-up views. Some leaves have small holes, likely from physical damage or minor insect activity, but no clear herbivory pattern is evident. The pink tag is an artificial marker, not a plant feature. The seedling is emerging from a litter layer, but no specific habitat details are discernible. Leaf surfaces are wet, possibly from recent rain, which enhances shine but does not affect structural assessment.
